# Draft:Battle Of Garni (1226)

----
Battle
The Battle of Garni took place in late 1226 as part of the ongoing Khwarezmian–Georgian War. Following Jalal al-Din Mangburnu's successful capture of Tbilisi earlier that year, Georgian nobles organized a coordinated ambush near Garni, using knowledge of the terrain and fortified positions. The Khwarezmian forces, though experienced and numerous, were decisively defeated by the Georgian army under the direction of Queen Rusudan and leading nobles such as Ivane Mkhargrdzeli and Shalva of Akhaltsikhe.
Aftermath
The defeat at Garni forced Jalal al-Din to retreat from central Georgia back toward Azerbaijan, abandoning the objective of permanent occupation. Georgian forces regained strategic initiative, consolidating defensive positions in Kartli and neighboring regions. The battle is considered a turning point in the war, demonstrating that Georgia, despite prior losses at Tbilisi, could still repel Khwarezmian invasions and maintain territorial integrity.
